scope: Pure inspector with original validators and two real-engine fixtures. No cloud service, crash test, hardware validation or unknown historical engine certification.

checks.name: Strict JSON refuses ambiguous duplicate fields, invalid syntax and excessive nesting
Transport inspection preserves exact original strings and inspects all 18 known keys
Outer checksum damage, future formats and oversize documents are refused
Historical UTF-16 value limits do not reject a valid Unicode backup as an 8 MiB byte overflow
A transport-readable but invalid nested replay is no longer mistaken for a valid game record
Nested malformed JSON, repeated keys and internal checksum damage are visible
Real Dossier slot envelopes retain their raw bytes and equal-revision divergence is flagged
Invalid frame commands, excessive duration and duplicate replay IDs are refused
Current, historical and missing replay contracts have distinct outcomes without playback claims
Comparing copies reports raw-setting differences and conflicting replay IDs without choosing a winner
Experimental replay produced by the real engine passes structure while simulation certification stays separate
A real main-match recording remains byte-identical after inspection and replays in its original current engine
